title: Proposal — Valemont Insurance Group AI Academy Cohort 2027
author: P024
summary: Proposal to Valemont Insurance Group for a 24-apprentice AI Academy cohort (AI & Automation Practitioner and Applied Machine Learning) funded from levy, plus commercial Copilot and AI governance add-ons.

version_history.change: First draft following discovery workshop on 24 September
Pricing and timeline added; reviewed by Dr Ben Hartley (curriculum)
Commercial discount and levy transfer option added
Final version submitted to Sally Miah

blocks.p: Valemont Insurance Group has asked Delcorn to help it build an in-house AI and automation capability across claims, underwriting and customer operations. This proposal sets out a **24-apprentice AI Academy cohort** starting in January 2027, funded entirely from Valemont's apprenticeship levy, supported by a programme of **commercial add-ons** that prepare leaders and teams to adopt Microsoft 365 Copilot safely.

kv: AI & Automation Practitioner (Level 4) x 16; Applied Machine Learning (Level 6) x 8

blocks.p: Valemont is already one of our largest partners, with {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM learners WHERE employer_id='EMP1002' AND status IN ('Active','Break in learning','Gateway','EPA')}} apprentices currently on programme. This cohort would make Valemont the largest AI Academy client in the financial services sector.
At the discovery workshop on 24 September 2026, Sally Miah, the Claims Transformation Director and the Group Data Protection Officer described three priorities:

numbered: **Automate low-value claims handling work** — around 38% of first-notification-of-loss activity is re-keying and triage that could be automated.
**Grow a pipeline of in-house machine-learning talent** for pricing and fraud models, reducing reliance on contractors (currently 11 contractor data scientists).
**Adopt Copilot responsibly** — 2,400 Microsoft 365 Copilot licences are being deployed from February 2027 and the board wants assurance on governance and benefits tracking.

blocks.p: Valemont also has unspent levy: its annual levy is {{sql:SELECT annual_levy_gbp FROM employers WHERE employer_id='EMP1002'|gbp}} and Sally indicated that funds are expiring each month. Valemont would like to use part of its transfer allowance to support apprenticeships in its approved repair network (see section 6).

For 16 colleagues from claims operations, customer service and finance. Over 15 months apprentices learn to identify automation opportunities, build and govern Power Automate and Copilot Studio solutions, and measure benefits. Each apprentice delivers a workplace automation project assessed at end-point assessment.

For 8 analysts from pricing and counter-fraud with strong quantitative backgrounds. A 24-month programme covering supervised learning, model evaluation, MLOps and responsible AI, culminating in a production-quality model project.

table.caption: Table 1 — Programmes proposed

bullets: Fully remote delivery: a named skills coach for every apprentice, monthly 1:1 coaching and 12-weekly tripartite progress reviews with the line manager.
Live online workshops in small cohorts, recorded for catch-up, using anonymised Valemont scenarios agreed with your Data Protection Officer.
Off-the-job training planned at an average of 6 hours per week and logged in the Aptiva e-portfolio, with a monthly OTJ report to Valemont.
Quarterly business reviews with Ravi Sharma covering starts, progress RAG, OTJ, withdrawals risk and learner NPS.

rows: Valemont decision and Employer Services Agreement signed
Levy commitments created in DAS / transfer agreed
table.caption: Table 2 — Indicative timeline

blocks.p: Apprenticeship training and end-point assessment are paid in full from Valemont's levy account. There is no additional cost to Valemont for apprenticeship delivery. Payments are drawn monthly by the Department for Education over the life of each apprenticeship, with 20% held back until completion.
Commercial items are invoiced on delivery, are subject to VAT at the standard rate and are payable within 30 days. Prices are taken from the Delcorn Pricing & Commercial Offer Sheet 2026/27.

Valemont can transfer up to 50% of its annual levy funds to other employers. We propose that Valemont pledges transfer funding for up to **12 Team Leader (Level 3)** apprenticeships across three repair-network partners. Delcorn will manage the transfer request process in the Digital Apprenticeship Service with each receiving employer; the receiving employers pay no co-investment.

blocks.callout: Levy funds expire 24 months after they enter the DAS account. Committing this cohort before 31 December 2026 would use funds that would otherwise expire between January and June 2027.
blocks.title: Why now

blocks.p: Since 2019 Delcorn has trained data analysts and team leaders across the Trust. In 2025/26, 26 apprentices completed and 40 end-point assessment results included 11 distinctions. Analysts built a theatre-utilisation dashboard now used daily by surgical directorates.

Kestrel's Data Foundations and Data Analyst apprentices automated depot performance reporting, saving an estimated 1,900 hours of manual reporting a year. 17 of 19 Kestrel leavers in 2025/26 achieved their apprenticeship.

bullets: Ofsted 'Strong standard' in all areas (February 2026).
Achievement rate of {{fact:achievement_rate_2526}} in 2025/26, well above the national average.
Learner Net Promoter Score of {{fact:learner_nps_12m}} over the last 12 months.
One of the first providers to deliver the Level 4 AI & Automation Practitioner programme (August 2026).

actions.action: Confirm preferred cohort sizes and start dates
Share draft Employer Services Agreement with Valemont procurement
Confirm transfer recipients and Team Leader numbers

author: P004
summary: How Delcorn finds, qualifies, proposes and closes employer partnerships: stages, qualification criteria, objection handling and PipelineHQ hygiene.

blocks.p: Our ideal partner is a UK employer with 250+ staff, a levy pot of £500,000 or more and a strategic need for AI, data, digital or leadership skills. Strategic accounts (Northgrid, Valemont, Brightwell, Halden Valley) are managed by named client partners; new business is led by Lewis Murray.

bullets: **L**evy: is the employer a levy payer? How much is unspent or expiring?
**E**xecutive sponsor: who owns the skills problem?
**V**alue: what business outcome will apprentices deliver?
**E**ligibility: do candidates meet funding rules (role, residency, prior learning)?
**R**eadiness: can line managers support off-the-job training?
Always start from the Proposal Template in the Proposals library.

title: Procurement Policy
author: P028
summary: How Delcorn buys goods and services: purchase order thresholds (£1k/£10k/£50k), approval levels, quotes, contracts, data protection and supplier payment.

version_history.change: Aligned with Meridian Education Group delegated authorities
Added AI tools and SaaS data protection check; clarified events spend

blocks.p: This policy applies to all staff who commit Delcorn to spend with external suppliers, including software subscriptions, events, contractors and agency staff. It ensures value for money, proper authorisation and compliance with Meridian Education Group delegated authorities.

bullets: **No PO, no pay**: a purchase order must be raised in Ledgerline and approved *before* the order is placed.
Spend must be within an approved cost-centre budget.
Orders must not be split to avoid an approval threshold.
Conflicts of interest must be declared to the Finance Manager.

columns: Order value (ex VAT, whole contract term)
rows: Head of department and Finance Manager
Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer
Formal tender or three quotes with evaluation; contract reviewed by Finance
As above, plus Meridian Education Group CFO
table.caption: Table 1 — Purchase order approval levels

blocks.callout: Thresholds apply to the total value over the contract term, not the annual value. A three-year £20,000-a-year software subscription is a £60,000 order and needs CEO and CFO approval.
blocks.title: Contract term matters

bullets: Contracts over £10,000 must be reviewed by Finance before signature; over £50,000 by the CFO.
All contracts are recorded in the Supplier Contract Renewals Tracker with an owner and end date.
Owners must start renewal or re-tender at least 90 days before the contract end date.

blocks.p: Any supplier that processes personal data must have a data processing agreement (DPA) in place before go-live, approved by the Data Protection Officer ({{person:P036}}). New AI tools also require approval under the AI acceptable use policy.

bullets: Invoices must quote a valid PO number and be sent to accounts.payable@delcorn.co.uk.
Delcorn pays valid, undisputed invoices within 30 days of receipt; payment runs are every Tuesday and Friday.
Invoices without a PO are returned to the supplier within 3 working days.
Bank detail changes must be verified by telephone using a known number before being updated.

blocks.p: Company cards may be used for purchases under £500 (subscriptions under £100 per month) and are reconciled monthly in Ledgerline with receipts.
Retrospective POs are reported monthly to the CFO. Repeated breaches may lead to card or approval rights being withdrawn and disciplinary action.

subject: Valemont AI Academy proposal — levy transfer and start dates
summary: Sally Miah (Valemont) and Ravi Sharma discuss the AI Academy proposal, cohort sizes, levy expiry and transferring levy to Valemont's repair-network partners.

messages.body:
Hi Sally,

Thank you again for hosting the discovery workshop. Please find attached our proposal for the AI Academy cohort.

In summary: 16 colleagues on the Level 4 AI & Automation Practitioner programme and 8 on the Level 6 Applied Machine Learning programme, a total levy value of £496,000, with first starts on 25 January 2027. We have also included the Executive AI Briefings, Copilot Adoption Bootcamps, a Responsible AI workshop and an AI Readiness Diagnostic as commercial add-ons, at £53,865 plus VAT after the volume discount.

Section 6 sets out how you could use your transfer allowance to fund Team Leader apprenticeships in your repair network.

Happy to walk your procurement team through it.

Best wishes,

Ravi

Hi Ravi,

Thanks — the exec team liked it. A few questions before we take it to our People Committee on 12 November:

1. Can we increase the AI & Automation cohort to 20 if demand from claims is strong? I have 31 expressions of interest.

2. On the levy transfer, our finance team say we have roughly £410k expiring between January and June. Can the transfer to our repair partners be set up before Christmas, and do they need to be your existing clients?

3. Is the 5% discount on the commercial items the best you can do, given we're a strategic account?

Thanks,

Sally

Hi Sally,

Great news. Answers below:

1. Yes — we can take up to 20 on the AI & Automation Practitioner cohort. That would increase the levy value by £76,000 to £572,000. We'd run two workshop groups of 10.

2. The receiving employers don't need to be existing Delcorn clients. Each partner creates a DAS account, you approve the transfer pledge, and we register the apprenticeships against it. If the partners can apply by 4 December, starts in January are realistic. Note that transfers can't be used for apprentices who already have the same qualification level.

3. As a Strategic account we can offer 10% on the commercial items, which would bring them to £51,030 plus VAT. I've checked this with Tom.

I'll send an updated version of the proposal by Friday.

Best wishes,

Ravi

Perfect, thank you Ravi. Please go with 20 on the AI cohort and the 10% discount. I'll send you the names of the three repair partners and their HR contacts on Monday.

Sally

Thanks Sally — noted. Ryan Fletcher (copied) will co-ordinate the transfer set-up with your partners and book candidate briefings for 1–11 December. Updated proposal (v1.4) to follow, and I'll send the draft Employer Services Agreement schedule to your procurement team on 10 November.

Best wishes,

Ravi

subject: P3 month-end — October funding variance

messages.body:
Andrew,

The draft P3 accounts show apprenticeship funding about £97k behind budget year to date, and October alone around £38k short. That's the second month running. Before I sign off the R03 return on Thursday, I need to understand what's timing and what's structural — and I don't want 'fewer starts' as the answer without numbers by academy.

Can you and Nicole give me a breakdown by tomorrow lunchtime?

Priya

Nicole,

Could you pull October and YTD funding by academy against the budget phasing (budget sheet in Budgets & Forecasts), and split the variance between on-programme and completion funding? I'll pick up the cost side.

Thanks,

Andrew

Hi both,

October funding was £752,080 against a £790,000 budget (−£37,920). YTD is £2,232,790 vs £2,330,000 (−£97,210). By academy YTD:

- Data Academy −£80.8k: the Northgrid Data Analyst cohort moved to January, and 11 completion payments slipped to November because EPA dates moved. Completion element is roughly £35k of this — timing.
- AI Academy −£24.8k: only 10 starts in October vs 21 last October. Employers waited for the new Level 4 launch pack. Partly structural unless the Valemont cohort lands.
- Digital −£20.3k and People −£3.1k: low starts, small numbers.
- Leadership +£31.8k: Operations Manager starts are absorbing former Senior Leader demand.

So I'd call around £35k timing and £62k structural/at risk. R03 validation is clean apart from two prior-learning warnings, which Daniel has checked.

Nicole

Thanks Nicole — that's exactly what I needed. Please put that split into the variance commentary sheet. Andrew, hold the full-year forecast at budget for now but add a downside scenario showing January starts slipping by 20%. I'll sign off R03 tomorrow morning.

Priya

subject: Overdue invoice BSE-4471 — Delcorn Skills Summit 24 September
summary: Brightside Events chases an unpaid invoice for the Skills Summit; Peter Walsh explains the PO mismatch, gets the variance approved and confirms payment date.

messages.body:
Dear Peter,

Our invoice BSE-4471 dated 25 September 2026 for £10,368.00 (including VAT) for the Delcorn Skills Summit on 24 September is now overdue. Our terms are 30 days. Could you let me know when we can expect payment?

Kind regards,

Karen Doyle
Credit Controller, Brightside Events

Dear Karen,

Thanks for getting in touch. We're holding invoice BSE-4471 because it doesn't match purchase order PO-26-0412, which was approved for £7,200 plus VAT (£8,640). The invoice is £8,640 plus VAT, so £1,440 higher, and we can't see an approved variation for the extra.

Could you send a breakdown of the additional charges? If they relate to the AV upgrade requested on the day, I'll ask our Marketing team to confirm and get the PO amended.

Kind regards,

Peter

Hi Peter,

Apologies — I should have attached it. The extra £1,440 is the AV upgrade (second screen and live-stream package) requested by Jess Morgan at 8.15am on the day, plus 12 additional lunches. Breakdown attached.

Karen

Dear Karen,

Thank you. Jess has confirmed the additional items and the PO has been amended to £8,640 net. As the total is now under £10,000 it stays within the Head of Department and Finance Manager approval level, and Andrew Clarke has approved it.

The invoice is scheduled for our payment run on Tuesday 4 November. Please note that, as your contract with us ends on 31 December, our Marketing team will be in touch about events for 2027.

Kind regards,

Peter
